svg.title: CAREN Apriori-style levelwise search over interval items
svg.desc: Itemset lattice where each item is a feature-interval condition; levelwise candidate generation with support pruning by anti-monotonicity, and the KS test as a second filter selecting distribution rules.
svg.text: CAREN — levelwise search over interval items
Each item is a feature ∈ quartile-interval condition. Support builds the lattice; the KS test selects the rules.
swa = pre-harvest soil water (mm) · rain_fl = wet days post-flowering · heat_sm = hot days pre-maturity · tmax_hv = max temp harvest (°C)
Anti-monotonicity — why it's tractable AND exhaustive (not greedy):
Adding an interval condition can only keep support equal or shrink it. So if an itemset is below min-support, every superset is too
— it is never generated (D and A∧C above). Within the frequent region CAREN keeps all candidates; a beam/greedy learner would
drop some and could miss A∧B. That completeness guarantee is CAREN's edge over decision-tree / beam rule learners.
